newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends modestly up in thin pre-API trade.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends modestly up in thin pre-API trade.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures ended modestly higher, but near the session lows, on a technical bounce ahead of this evening's American Petroleum Institute report.
But prices were locked into tight ranges and the price correction, following a roughly 10 percent drop in the last three weeks, was seen as fragile, barring any suprises in the API data.
"We basically have a market constricted from any great movement until the APIs are released," said one energy analyst.
March Brent closed up 20 cents at $22.25 a barrel after trading between $22.18, which was touched near the close, and $22.39.
The March/April spread did widen by about 11 cents to a 52-cent backwardation.

Buyers clung to the fact that it was able to hold a four-month low at $22 on the spot chart, but Brent posted an "inside trading day" by staying within its session range from Monday, reflecting a pause or consolidation.

"On the horizon, we have cold weather warnings and refinery turnarounds boosting opinions, tempered by talk of weak Asian demand producing product surpluses in a market that can usually be relied to take up the slack," the analyst said.
U.S. traders expected the API to be neutral for prices, with a distillate decline of about two million barrels, gasoline build of 2.25 million and a crude increase of three million.
Earlier, Feb gas oil ended 75 cents higher at $200.50 a tonne.
